blocks.text: I can explore the influence and presentation of religion through the character of Friar Lawrence in ‘Romeo and Juliet’.
You will look at how Shakespeare portrays Friar Lawrence and his influence, then think about what Shakespeare might be suggesting about religion and Catholicism.
Tap each word to see what it means.

items.def: the capacity to have an effect on the character, development, or behaviour of someone or something
to give a clear understanding or impression of: to describe or present clearly
the action or practice of deceiving someone by concealing or misrepresenting the truth
the faith, practice, and church order of the Roman Catholic Church

blocks.text: Friar Lawrence is an incredibly influential character in ‘Romeo and Juliet’. He has the capacity to affect the characters and their behaviour. He:

items: facilitates the marriage between Romeo and Juliet: he agrees to it and officially marries them
counsels Romeo to go to Mantua following Romeo’s banishment and agrees to send him news of Verona
provides Juliet with the potion that allows her to fake her own death

blocks.text: Throughout the play, we see Friar Lawrence influencing the lives and behaviour of characters.

slides.title: Is he responsible for the tragedy?

blocks.text: To what extent is Friar Lawrence responsible for the tragedy? He facilitates the marriage, he tries to hide the marriage by assisting Juliet in faking her own death, and he tells Romeo that he will send him news of Verona.

blocks.label: One pupil’s idea
blocks.text: We could say he is responsible: he facilitates the marriage that creates the chain of events leading to the tragic ending. If he had not agreed to marry Romeo and Juliet, then arguably their love story would have ended after the Capulet ball.
These are all hypotheticals, but they show us how much influence Friar Lawrence has on the tragic events.
When agreeing to marry Romeo and Juliet, Friar Lawrence says:
“For this alliance may so happy prove / To turn your households’ rancor to pure love.” (Act 2, Scene 3, lines 98-99)

Friar Lawrence is trying to provide a solution to a social problem: to end the feud between the Montagues and Capulets. We know from the Prince’s speech in Act 1, Scene 1 that the feud is negatively impacting society because of the fights that keep breaking out.

blocks.q: Which social problem is Friar Lawrence hoping the marriage might solve?
options: The feud between the Montagues and Capulets
blocks.why: He hopes the alliance will turn the households’ rancor to pure love, ending the feud.

blocks.text: We might think of Friar Lawrence as **representing** religion in ‘Romeo and Juliet’. His character gives us a clear understanding of religion at the time.
If he represents religion, what might Shakespeare be saying about the influence of religion on society? Tap for one idea.

blocks.label: Tap for an idea
blocks.text: Perhaps that religion was able to exert great influence over people’s lives and the course their lives took. Although the feud is solved by the marriage, Romeo and Juliet’s lives are the price paid for peace, which could represent how religious influence focuses on the big picture rather than the concerns of individuals.
Arguably, Friar Lawrence represents religion in ‘Romeo and Juliet’. Religion was at the very heart of government in Elizabethan England.

slides.title: A mentor, or something more negative?

blocks.text: Friar Lawrence is often seen as a mentor and father figure to Romeo, because Romeo confides in him and seeks his advice. However, we might also consider his portrayal in a more negative light:

items: Friar Lawrence is aware of Romeo and Juliet’s marriage but does not say anything to their parents.
Friar Lawrence allows Juliet to fake her own death rather than admit that she cannot marry Count Paris because he married her to Romeo.

blocks.text: What might this suggest about his character?

items.def: the action or practice of deceiving someone by concealing or misrepresenting the truth

blocks.text: We might interpret Friar Lawrence’s character as being deceitful. Though he is aware of the marriage between Romeo and Juliet, he does not share this information with their parents, even when it would have been useful to do so.

blocks.label: One pupil’s idea
blocks.text: It suggests that Friar Lawrence is capable of being deceitful and secretive, and that he is willing to put his own interests before the interests of others: he could have admitted to Lord Capulet that Juliet is already married, yet he does not do so.
In Act 5, Scene 3, despite finding Romeo dead, Friar Lawrence abandons Juliet in the tomb because:
“a noise did scare me from the tomb” (line 271)

blocks.label: What perception might this create?
blocks.text: It could create the perception that Friar Lawrence is cowardly. It adds to the idea that he places his own self-interest before the interests of others.
When consoling Romeo after his banishment, Friar Lawrence says:
“Art thou a man? Thy form cries out thou art. / Thy tears are womanish” (Act 3, Scene 3, lines 119-120)

blocks.q: By asking “Art thou a man?”, what is Friar Lawrence questioning?
blocks.why: By specifically asking if Romeo is a “man”, Friar Lawrence implies that his actions suggest he is not one, so he is questioning his masculinity.

blocks.text: This also implies religious influence on the societal pressure of gender stereotypes.
Though never explicitly stated, we can arguably see Friar Lawrence as representing {Catholicism}:

items: a “Friar” is a man belonging to any of the Roman Catholic religious orders
‘Romeo and Juliet’ is set in Verona, and the predominant religion of Italy in the Elizabethan Era was Catholicism

blocks.text: What might Shakespeare be saying about Catholicism through this portrayal? He may have been presenting Catholicism as acting in its own self-interest and allowing others to suffer the consequences of its actions. He may also have been presenting Catholicism as adding to societal expectations of gender through Friar Lawrence’s presentation of Romeo’s masculinity.

items: There were deep religious divides between Catholicism and Protestantism at the time.
Queen Elizabeth I was Protestant; however, her predecessor, Queen Mary I, was Catholic.
To strengthen her position, Queen Elizabeth I passed laws to try to minimise the Catholic threat.
However, there were continual threats throughout her reign from those who wished to replace her with a Catholic monarch.

blocks.why: Queen Elizabeth I was Protestant; her predecessor, Queen Mary I, was Catholic.

blocks.text: Queen Elizabeth I faced constant threats to her person and her throne from Catholic sympathisers and tried to minimise their influence. Arguably, she would have wanted Catholicism to be represented negatively in literature.
Arguably, we might consider Shakespeare to have represented Catholicism through Friar Lawrence in a way that Queen Elizabeth I would have approved of. What are the implications? Tap for two ideas.

blocks.label: Two ideas
blocks.text: Perhaps Shakespeare was writing in a way to preserve the status quo, because a monarch would not want society to desire change. Or perhaps his intentions were to produce literature that the monarch approved of, to continue to have their favour.

blocks.q: Which idea does each action support?

items.text: He officially marries Romeo and Juliet
He counsels Romeo to go to Mantua
He agrees to send Romeo news of Verona
He does not tell their parents about the marriage
He leaves Juliet in the tomb because “a noise did scare me from the tomb”

items.q: A “Friar” is a man belonging to which group?
options: Any of the Roman Catholic religious orders

items.q: Which religion was predominant in Italy in the Elizabethan Era?
Friar Lawrence hopes the marriage will turn the households’ rancor into what?

items: Arguably, Friar Lawrence represents religion in ‘Romeo and Juliet’.
Throughout the play, we see Friar Lawrence influencing the lives and behaviour of characters.
Potentially, we might see Shakespeare as criticising the influence of religion on society through Friar Lawrence.
Furthermore, we might see Shakespeare as criticising Catholicism through Friar Lawrence.

worksheet.title: Worksheet: ‘Romeo and Juliet’: exploring the influence of religion on society
worksheet.instructions: Answer each question with a word or a short phrase.

questions.prompt: Friar Lawrence has the capacity to affect the characters and their behaviour. Which keyword names this? (one word)
questions.explanation: Influence means the capacity to have an effect on the character, development, or behaviour of someone or something.

questions.prompt: After Romeo’s banishment, to which place does Friar Lawrence counsel him to go?
questions.explanation: He counsels Romeo to go to Mantua and agrees to send him news of Verona.

questions.prompt: What does Friar Lawrence provide for Juliet that allows her to fake her own death?
questions.explanation: He provides Juliet with the potion that allows her to fake her own death.

questions.prompt: Complete the line from Act 5, Scene 3: “a noise did scare me from the ______”.
questions.explanation: Friar Lawrence abandons Juliet in the tomb because of a noise.

questions.prompt: Which noun means the action or practice of deceiving someone by concealing or misrepresenting the truth?
questions.explanation: Friar Lawrence keeping the marriage from the parents can be interpreted as deceitful.

questions.prompt: Complete Friar Lawrence’s line: “To turn your households’ ______ to pure love.”
questions.explanation: He hopes the marriage will end the feud between the Montagues and Capulets.

questions.prompt: Which religion was predominant in Italy, where the play is set, in the Elizabethan Era?
questions.explanation: Catholicism was the predominant religion of Italy at that time.

questions.prompt: Which queen was Protestant: Elizabeth I or Mary I?
questions.explanation: Queen Elizabeth I was Protestant; her predecessor Queen Mary I was Catholic.

questions.prompt: Which queen, Elizabeth I’s predecessor, was Catholic?
questions.explanation: Queen Elizabeth I’s predecessor, Queen Mary I, was Catholic.
